title: Baked Beans – Best Ever
description:
Whoa, Nelly (or Ree Drummond, The Pioneer Women). I never knew baked beans could be this good. I never
knew baked beans could be improved upon. I never knew baked beans could be such a triumph, such a prayer,
such a song. But they can. I now know they can.
Pam Anderson – sometimes called "Pamanderson" just to conserve energy – whipped these up (with some of my
own modifications). What makes these the best baked beans ever? First and foremost, these baked beans are easy
to make. They start with 3 big ol' cans of regular pork and beans, but it's the other ingredients you add that
transforms them! That brings me to my next point: the other stuff. This recipe is filled with tangy barbecue sauce,
sweet brown sugar, mustard for a kick, onion, and maybe (definitely) the best addition of all—bacon! The beans
are topped with strips of partially-cooked bacon, and baked low and slow until the bacon gets a little crispy and
the beans thicken. The result is baked beans that are smoky, sweet, tangy, and absolutely unforgettable! You'll
never make them any other way.
ingredients: 8 slices bacon, cut to bite sizes
1/4 cup cider or rice or white wine vinegar
2 tsp. dry mustard or 2 tbsp. Dijon
directions: Adjust oven rack to lower-middle position and heat oven to 350°.
Fry bacon in large, deep sauté pan until bacon has partially cooked and released about 1/4 cup drippings.
Remove bacon from pan and drain on paper towels. Use some of the bacon fat to grease the baking dish.
Add onion to drippings in pan and sauté until tender, about 5 minutes. Add the garlic a cook for less than a
Add beans and remaining ingredients to pan; bring to a simmer. (If pan is not large enough, add beans and
heat to a simmer then transfer to a large bowl and stir in remaining ingredients).
Pour flavored beans into a greased 13-by-9-inch (or similar size) ovenproof pan.
Top with bacon, then bake until beans the sauce is the consistency of very thick pancake syrup, about 1 to
1½ hours. You want the beans to be very, very cooked, the bacon very, very brown, and no soupiness to
Let stand to thicken slightly and serve.
